label: Third/fourth original input (t=2,3), gated by token identity (a, t, q, b, ...)
explanation: Strictly positional reset-gate unit: 99% of activations (and 99% of mass) fall on original-phase steps t=2 and t=3 (70% of mass at t=2, 30% at t=3); it essentially never fires at t=0,1, t>=4, or in the copy phase, and only weakly on the <DEL> step when L=3. Position alone gives recall 0.99 but precision 0.32 (fires on 43% of t=2 steps, 21% of t=3 steps). Which of those steps fire depends on the input token and context: a and t are strongest (rate ~3x), then q, b, k, s, d, 0, m, j, c, z; first occurrences of a token are favored (93% of mass on in_first). Top activations are a at t=2 after contexts like e y / n y / v y (prev token y, first token e boost). Restricting to the 12 highest-lift tokens gives dev P 0.58, R 0.70, mass recall 0.80; the remaining token/context dependence was not captured.
